{{Short description|Norwegian chemist (1936–2023)}}
{{distinguish|Arne Wegner Haaland}}

'''Arne Haaland''' (15 February 1936 – 13 October 2023) was a [[Norway|Norwegian]] chemist.

Haaland received his PhD in philosophy from the University of Oslo in 1969 and was an [[associate professor]] in chemistry at the University of Oslo from 1964 to 1984, and then a professor until his retirement.<ref name="snl">{{cite encyclopedia|title=Arne Haaland|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|url=http://www.snl.no/Arne_Haaland|language=no|access-date=12 September 2012}}</ref> He was a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dnva.no/medlemmer/15|title=Norske medlemmer|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=no|access-date=27 December 2021}}</ref>

Haaland ran a laboratory for [[gas electron diffraction]]. He, his co-workers and colleagues determined the structures of umpteen important chemical compounds in the gas phase. His main field of research was the [[Organometallic chemistry|organometallic]] compounds.

The list of such structure determinations includes the controversially debated beryllocene,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Almenningen|first1=A.|last2=Bastiansen|first2=O.|last3=Haaland|first3=A.|date=June 1964|title=Molecular Structure of Dicyclopentadienylberyllium (C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>2</sub>Be|url=http://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.1725019|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|language=en|volume=40|issue=11|pages=3434–3437|doi=10.1063/1.1725019|bibcode=1964JChPh..40.3434A|issn=0021-9606|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=Haaland1968>{{Cite journal|last=Haaland|first=Arne|title=On the Molecular Structure of Di-cyclopentadienylberyllium (C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>5</sub>)<sub>2</sub>Be. II. Least Squares Refinement|date=1968|url=|journal=Acta Chemica Scandinavica|volume=22|pages=3030–3032|doi=10.3891/acta.chem.scand.22-3030|doi-access=free}}</ref> dibenzene chromium,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Haaland|first1=A.|last2=Blomstrand|first2=Rolf|last3=Reunanen|first3=Matti|last4=Kyyhkynen|first4=Hertta|last5=Hoffman|first5=Ragnar A.|last6=Westerdahl|first6=Anders|date=1965|title=The Molecular Structure of Gaseous Dibenzene Chromium (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>6</sub>)<sub>2</sub>Cr|journal=Acta Chemica Scandinavica|volume=19|pages=41–46|doi=10.3891/acta.chem.scand.19-0041|issn=0904-213X|doi-access=free}}</ref> ferrocene,<ref name=Haaland1968/> the structure of the phosphorus oxides P<sub>4</sub>O<sub>10</sub> and P<sub>4</sub>O<sub>9</sub>, trimethylamuminium<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Almenningen|first1=A.|last2=Halvorsen|first2=S.|last3=Haaland|first3=A.|last4=Pihlaja|first4=Kalevi|last5=Schaumburg|first5=Kjeld|last6=Ehrenberg|first6=L.|date=1971|title=A Gas Phase Electron Diffraction Investigation of the Molecular Structures of Trimethylaluminium Monomer and Dimer.|journal=Acta Chemica Scandinavica|language=en|volume=25|pages=1937–1945|doi=10.3891/acta.chem.scand.25-1937|issn=0904-213X|doi-access=free}}</ref> and its adducts with NMe<sub>3</sub>,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Anderson|first=G. A.|date=1971|title=MOLECULAR STRUCTURE OF TRIMETHYLALUMINIUM-TRIMETHYLAMINE BY ELECTRON DIFFRACTION|url=|journal=Journal of the Chemical Society D: Chemical Communications|volume=|pages=480|via=}}</ref> and the first stable silylene.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Denk|first1=Michael|last2=Lennon|first2=Robert|last3=Hayashi|first3=Randy|last4=West|first4=Robert|last5=Belyakov|first5=Alexander V.|last6=Verne|first6=Hans P.|last7=Haaland|first7=Arne|last8=Wagner|first8=Matthias|last9=Metzler|first9=Nils|date=March 1994|title=Synthesis and Structure of a Stable Silylene|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja00085a088|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=en|volume=116|issue=6|pages=2691–2692|doi=10.1021/ja00085a088|bibcode=1994JAChS.116.2691D |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Haaland was the author of many contributions on chemical bonding,<ref>{{Cite book|last=Haaland, Arne.|title=Molecules and models : the molecular structures of main group element compounds|date=2008|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-923535-3|location=Oxford|oclc=173809048}}</ref> in particular the dative bond<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Haaland|first=Arne|date=August 1989|title=Covalent versus Dative Bonds to Main Group Metals, a Useful Distinction|url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/anie.198909921|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English|language=en|volume=28|issue=8|pages=992–1007|doi=10.1002/anie.198909921|issn=0570-0833|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and metallocenes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Haaland|first=Arne|date=1979-11-01|title=Molecular structure and bonding in the 3d metallocenes|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ar50143a006|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|language=en|volume=12|issue=11|pages=415–422|doi=10.1021/ar50143a006|issn=0001-4842|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
